'''Béarnaise sauce''' is an egg-yolk and butter emulsion in the [[Cookbook:Hollandaise|Hollandaise]] family of sauces. 

== Ingredients ==
* 30 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]]) tarragon [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* 30 ml (2 tablespoons) [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]] [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] or dry white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Egg yolk|egg yolks]]
* 75–100 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (⅓–½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] / 3–4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (warm but not hot)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|Cayenne pepper]] to taste
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] freshly-chopped [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]]
* 1 tablespoon freshly-chopped [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]

== Procedure ==

# Put the vinegars, shallot, and herbs in a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]; [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until reduced to 1 tablespoon. This is the flavorful glaze. Strain and set aside to cool.
# Add the egg yolks and [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] until the ribbon stage with a balloon whisk.
# Place the bowl over a pan of hot water (a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]]) and continue whisking. Gradually add the melted butter, whisking until the sauce thickens and all the butter has been added.
# Season and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Do not use dried tarragon; if you cannot find fresh tarragon, use a sprig from the vinegar bottle.
* To find the right temperature to [[Cookbook:Emulsification|emulsify]] the egg mixture and the butter, the bowl should be just hot enough so that you can still touch it. If you cannot hold the bowl it is too hot. Be forewarned that this trick may not always work depending on a multitude of conditions.

==References==
* Julia Child (1961), ''Mastering the Art of French Cooking'', Alfred A. Knopf
